question.text: An AIF proposes to appoint an independent valuer for unlisted-security valuation through the IBBI Registered Valuer / Registered Valuer Entity route described in the workbook. Which framework primarily governs that valuer's registration and conduct?

answer.text: Only SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012, with no role for any other regulator
Registration as an IBBI Registered Valuer (individual) with ICAI/ICSI/ICMAI/CFA professional membership, or as an IBBI Registered Valuer Entity with authorised-person membership
ICAI alone, under a Chartered Accountants Act notification
RBI under the Banking Regulation Act

explanation.text: The Logic: When the AIF chooses the IBBI route, the workbook requires that an individual valuer be registered with IBBI and hold membership of ICAI, ICSI, ICMAI, or the CFA Institute, and that an entity valuer hold IBBI Registered Valuer Entity status with authorised-person membership. SEBI overlays AIF-specific eligibility (experience and non-associate requirements) on top of this IBBI framework. The Trap: Option A treats SEBI as the sole framework, missing the IBBI registration requirement. Option C narrows the framework to a single professional body. Option D names the wrong regulator. Note: The IBBI route described here is one of the eligible routes in the workbook; the workbook separately recognises alternatives such as a holding/subsidiary of a SEBI-registered Credit Rating Agency or other SEBI-specified criteria for the valuer.
